transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, what brought me in is... I just don't feel like myself anymore. It's hard to explain, but I barely talk to people lately. I just go flat, you know? Quiet. Even getting started on my cleaning route at the building feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. And speaking of carts, they gave us these new ones last month, supposed to be ergonomic or something, but the wheels squeak constantly. Squeak, squeak, squeak, all down the third-floor hallway. It drives you nuts if you think about it too much. I tried WD-40, but the maintenance guy, Carl—he’s been there twenty years, thinks he owns the place—he said I wasn't allowed to fix the carts myself. Union rules or something. But anyway, yeah, I just... I can't seem to get going, and I'm just so quiet all the time now.
How long have you been feeling this way—flat, quiet, and low on energy—has it been days, weeks, or longer?

Well, it's been... let's see. The depression part, the feeling low and flat, that's been with me for about a year and two months now. Yeah, it started not long after the move. We moved apartments because the rent kept going up at the old place, which is just how it goes in this city, right? They slap a coat of paint on the lobby and suddenly they want another three hundred dollars a month. So we moved to this new place over on 4th Street. It's got a nice little bakery on the corner. The guy who runs it, Sal, he makes these incredible almond croissants. My wife loves them. We used to go every Sunday morning, grab a coffee, sit by the window... but I haven't been in months. I just don't have the energy for it. Sal probably thinks we moved away again. But yeah, about a year and two months.
Over this past year and two months, has your low mood and lack of energy stayed pretty much the same the whole time, or have there been certain stretches where it got noticeably worse than others?

Well, it's... it's mostly just been there the whole time. For most of the time since the move, that sadness, the low energy, feeling guilty about everything, and just not caring about things I used to... it's just been there in the background. Even on days when the voices were really loud, or when I was so worried about the cameras... the cameras they installed in the breakroom, you know? They said it was for security, because someone kept taking the good coffee creamer. Which, I mean, is ridiculous. It's just creamer. But they put these little black domes up in the corners, and they blink. Just this tiny red light, blinking, blinking. I told Carl it was an invasion of privacy, but he just laughed at me. Said if I wasn't stealing the French vanilla, I had nothing to worry about. But you never know who's watching those feeds, right? Could be anybody sitting in a dark room somewhere just... watching us eat our sandwiches. But yeah, even when I'm stressed about all that, or hearing the voices, the heavy, sad feeling is still just... always sitting there underneath it all.

Have you ever experienced the voices or the feeling that you're being watched during times when your mood was actually okay—not sad or low—or do they only happen when you're already feeling depressed?

Well, actually, there was a time... a stretch of several weeks where I felt a bit better. My mood had lifted some, you know? I was getting through my meals, getting through work a little easier. I even thought about going back to Sal's bakery, maybe just for a plain coffee, not the croissant. Sal's a good guy, he always asks about my wife. He used to be a mechanic before he opened the bakery, if you can believe it. Used to work on those old vintage cars, the ones with the big tail fins. He said he got tired of the grease under his fingernails, so he traded it for flour. Flour's easier to wash off, I guess. But anyway, even during those weeks when I felt okay, I... I still heard my name being called in the stairwell at work. Just echoing down the steps. And I was still absolutely convinced those hallway cameras were tracking me. Even when I wasn't feeling so down, they were still watching. Just... tracking every move.
That stretch of several weeks when your mood was better but you still heard your name called and felt watched—about how many weeks did that period last?

Well, it was... let's see, it was probably about three weeks, maybe four? Yeah, a few weeks where the heavy feeling wasn't there so much. I remember because I was actually getting through my meals, and the cleaning at work wasn't dragging me down as bad. I was sweeping the main lobby—it's a big lobby, marble floors, you know? You have to use a special cleaner on marble or it loses its shine. The guy who had the job before me, he used the wrong stuff once and stripped the finish right off a patch near the elevators. They had to bring in a specialist from out of state to buff it out. Cost a fortune, I heard. But anyway, yeah, for those few weeks, I felt a little better, but... I was still hearing it. My name, just echoing in that concrete stairwell when I was mopping. And those cameras in the hall, I knew they were still tracking me. Even when I wasn't feeling so sad, they were still watching. Every step.

Thinking back before the move and before you started feeling depressed—did you ever hear your name called or feel like you were being watched, or did all of that begin around the same time as the low mood a year and two months ago?

Well, no, it wasn't before the move. The move was... what, a year and two months ago? But the voices and the worries about the cameras, that's been going on for about 11 months now. It started after we'd been in the new place for a little while. The new place is nice, though. It's got this big bay window in the living room. My wife put all her African violets there. She's got quite a collection. Started with just one little pot her sister gave her for our anniversary—our 25th, I think it was. Now she's got purple ones, pink ones, even one that's got sort of ruffled edges on the leaves. She spends hours just watering them from the bottom, you know, you can't get the leaves wet or they rot. It's a whole science. She even talks to them sometimes, says it helps them grow. But anyway, yeah, the voices and feeling watched, that started about 11 months ago, a few months after we got settled in.
During those three or four weeks when you felt better, were you completely free of the sadness and low feelings, or did you still notice some of that heaviness, just to a lesser degree?

Well, I was completely free of it, yeah. The sadness was gone. Like I said, it was a stretch of several weeks where my mood had lifted. I felt okay, getting through my meals fine, and work was a little better. I even started taking my lunch breaks outside on the loading dock instead of hiding in the utility closet. The loading dock gets good sun around noon. There's this stray cat that hangs around out there, an orange tabby. Poor thing's missing half its left ear. I started bringing little scraps of tuna from home to leave out for him. Not the cheap tuna, either, the solid white albacore. My wife buys it in bulk from that warehouse club we joined. You know, the one where you have to show a card at the door? They have these huge jars of pickles there, too, like you'd see in a deli. I don't know who eats that many pickles. But anyway, yeah, the heaviness was completely gone for those weeks. I felt pretty good. But... I still heard my name in that stairwell. And I was still absolutely convinced those hallway cameras were being used to track me. Even without the sadness, they were still watching.

This pattern fulfills schizoaffective disorder criteria and argues against primary schizophrenia (mood symptoms are too prominent/persistent) and against MDD with psychotic features (psychosis outlasts mood episode).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a major depressive syndrome (low mood, anergia, guilt, anhedonia) lasting over a year, concurrent with persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of his name being called, delusional beliefs of being watched/tracked via cameras) present for about 11 months. Critically, there was a clearly documented 3-4 week period during which the depressive symptoms fully remitted while the hallucinations and delusions persisted unabated, confirming that psychotic symptoms occur independent of the mood episode for a significant duration. This pattern—mood episode overlapping with psychosis for the majority of the illness course, plus psychotic symptoms present for ≥2 weeks in the absence of mood symptoms—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type, rather than Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief relative to psychotic illness duration).
